pencereler.0-5: Seventy-three seconds after launch, Challenger broke apart. Seven astronauts were killed, in front of
pencereler.5-12: the world. The cause was just a rubber ring, a quarter-inch thick. Overnight, temperatures fell well below freezing. Cold
pencereler.12-20: made the O-rings stiff, so they couldn't seal the booster joint. Burning gas escaped the joint and cut into the fuel tank.
pencereler.20-30: Engineers had warned against launching in the cold the night before. They were overruled. Today, that warning is taught to every engineer.

segmentler.metin: The Space Shuttle Challenger broke apart 73 seconds after launch.
It took only an O-ring seal stiffened by cold.
So how could an O-ring seal stiffened by cold do this?
The answer is O-ring seal failure in a solid rocket booster field joint — and it is why NASA redesigned the booster joints and changed how engineering objections are heard before launch.
